#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#
# --hint=nomultithread
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a direct batch directive for controlling CPU binding
#   hints like disabling multithreading. This is typically managed via system
#   configuration or through the launcher (e.g., 'flux run --cpu-affinity=...').
#   Performance implication: Without this hint, Flux may schedule tasks on
#   hyperthreads of the same physical core, which could lead to resource contention
#   and reduced performance for CPU-intensive applications.
#
# -C a100
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a standard batch directive for resource constraints
#   or features. This is typically handled at submission time with a requirement,
#   e.g., 'flux submit --requires=a100 ...'.
#   Performance implication: Without the constraint, the job may be scheduled on a
#   node that does not have the required 'a100' feature (e.g., a different GPU
#   model), which would cause the application to fail or perform sub-optimally.
#

#   Omitted. Flux does not have a direct equivalent to redirect output from the
#   'flux run' command itself. Shell redirection should be used on the command line.

## load environment
module purge
module load cpuarch/amd
module load anaconda-py3/2023.03
conda activate claire

## launch script on every node
set -x

MODEL=tiiuae/falcon-7b
OUTDIR=$WORK/../commun/Claire/pretrain/Claire-7B-0.1_1
mkdir -p $OUTDIR

# The SLURM 'srun' command is replaced by 'flux run'. 'flux run' will automatically
# launch the 2 tasks requested by the '#FLUX: -n 2' directive. Shell redirection
# is used to capture output and error streams.

--devices 2 \
--num_nodes 1 \
--data_dir $SCRATCH/../commun/preprocessed_data/Claire/lit-gpt/padded_8_grouped/$MODEL \

--language fr \
--out_dir $OUTDIR \
--precision bf16-true \
--num_epochs 1000 \
--max_checkpoints 39 \
--enable_validation true \
--save_interval 1800 \
--eval_interval 1800 \
--early_stopping 4 \
--lora_r 16 \
--lora_alpha 32 > "$OUTDIR/training_log.out" 2>&1
